draft.title: Alcohols
card: An alcohol has a hydroxyl group, OH, bonded to a carbon atom in a carbon chain. Names end in -ol, such as ethanol and propan-2-ol.
the carbon bonded to the OH group is attached to one other carbon atom, as in propan-1-ol.
the carbon bonded to the OH group is attached to two other carbon atoms, as in propan-2-ol.

the carbon bonded to the OH group is attached to three other carbon atoms, as in 2-methylpropan-2-ol. Alcohols have higher boiling points than alkanes of similar size, because OH groups form hydrogen bonds between molecules. These take more energy to break than the dispersion forces between alkane molecules.
draft.remember: Type depends on the carbon holding the OH. Hydrogen bonding raises boiling points.

a.q: Why does ethanol have a higher boiling point than ethane?
opts: Ethanol molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other
Ethanol molecules have covalent bonds and ethane has none
Ethanol has a longer carbon chain than ethane
Ethanol molecules break apart when heated, ethane does not
a.why: The OH group in ethanol forms hydrogen bonds between molecules, and these need more energy to break than the dispersion forces in ethane. Ethane also has covalent bonds, so that is not the difference.
a.clue: Think about the forces between molecules, not the bonds inside them.

b.q: Butan-2-ol has the structure CH3CH(OH)CH2CH3. How is it classified, and why?
opts: Secondary, as the carbon with OH is bonded to two carbons
Primary, as the OH group is near the end of the chain
Secondary, as the molecule has two carbons after the OH
Tertiary, as the carbon with OH has three bonds to atoms
b.why: The carbon holding the OH is bonded to one CH3 and one CH2CH3, so it is attached to two other carbons. That makes it secondary. Counting all carbons in the molecule, or the position in the chain, does not decide the type.
b.clue: Count only the carbon atoms attached to the carbon that holds the OH.

a.best: Ethanol molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other

b.best: Secondary, as the carbon with OH is bonded to two carbons

problems.detail: The primary definition says the OH carbon is attached to one other carbon atom. Methanol, whose OH carbon is attached to no other carbons, is also classed as primary. The definition should say 'one or no other carbon atoms'. Likewise, 'bonded to a carbon atom in a carbon chain' does not fit methanol.
The boiling point explanation is joined onto the tertiary bullet, so a student could read it as applying only to tertiary alcohols. It belongs in its own bullet.

proposal.title: Alcohols
card: An alcohol has a hydroxyl group, OH, bonded to a carbon atom. Names end in -ol, such as ethanol and propan-2-ol.
Primary alcohols have one or no other carbon atoms attached to the carbon holding the OH, as in methanol and propan-1-ol.
Secondary alcohols have two other carbons attached to that carbon, as in propan-2-ol. Tertiary alcohols have three, as in 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

Alcohols boil at higher temperatures than alkanes of similar size. Their OH groups form hydrogen bonds between molecules, which take more energy to break than the dispersion forces between alkane molecules.
